node.title: Re: When does IPC::Open\d work on Windows, and when doesn't?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Unfortunately I don't have a Windows machine handy at the moment, so I can't answer your question directly. The [mod://IPC::Run3] docs do say this:

For each redirector $stdin, $stdout, and $stderr, run3() furnishes a filehandle: if the redirector already specifies a filehandle it just uses that

Running the following test on Linux with [man://strace] appears to show this is true even for Perl's in-memory filehandles:

use warnings; use strict; use IPC::Run3 'run3'; my $in = "Foo\nBar\n"; my $out = ""; # This uses temp files: #run3 ['/bin/cat'], \$in, \$out or die "run3"; open my $infh, '<', \$in or die $!; open my $outfh, '>', \$out or die $!; run3 ['/bin/cat'], $infh, $outfh or die "run3"; $?==0 or die "$?";

If that doesn't work, you might also want to give [mod://IPC::Run] a try.

AFAIK many IPC modules have similar issues on Windows, I think that's part of the reason why [mod://IPC::Run3] uses temporary files often - it's more reliable (just compare the CPAN Testers Matrix of [mod://IPC::Run3] with any other IPC module).

BTW, you're worried about efficiency, but haven't said what kind of a load you're expecting - are you sure this isn't premature optimization?
